questions.stem: A 58-year-old man presents with substernal chest pressure radiating to the left arm that began 40 minutes ago. ECG shows 2-mm ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Which artery is most likely occluded?

A 24-year-old woman with asthma reports worsening nocturnal cough despite daily inhaled corticosteroid use. Spirometry shows FEV1 72% predicted with 14% bronchodilator response. What is the best next step in management?
A 67-year-old man with type 2 diabetes has a serum creatinine of 2.1 mg/dL and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 480 mg/g. Which medication class provides the greatest renoprotective benefit?

A 33-year-old woman presents with heat intolerance, palpitations, and a 6-kg weight loss. TSH is suppressed and free T4 is elevated. A diffusely enlarged, nontender thyroid is palpated. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man with chronic alcohol use presents with hematemesis. Endoscopy reveals bleeding esophageal varices. After resuscitation, which pharmacologic agent should be started to reduce portal pressure?

A 29-year-old returning traveler from sub-Saharan Africa presents with cyclical fevers, headache, and thrombocytopenia. A thin blood smear shows ring forms within erythrocytes. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
A 71-year-old woman presents with fatigue and a hemoglobin of 8.4 g/dL. MCV is 68 fL, ferritin is 6 ng/mL. What is the most likely underlying cause to investigate next?

A 52-year-old woman reports symmetric morning stiffness lasting 90 minutes affecting the MCP and PIP joints. Anti-CCP and rheumatoid factor are positive. Which finding most strongly predicts erosive disease?
A 63-year-old man develops sudden right-sided weakness and expressive aphasia. CT head is unremarkable at 90 minutes from onset. Blood pressure is 168/92 mmHg. What is the most appropriate next step?
A 19-year-old presents with a well-demarcated, salmon-colored plaque with silvery scale over the extensor elbows. Pinpoint bleeding occurs when scale is removed. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old man with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 28%) remains symptomatic on lisinopril, carvedilol, and spironolactone. Which intervention provides the greatest mortality benefit?
A 40-year-old woman presents with episodic flushing, diarrhea, and wheezing. Urinary 5-HIAA is markedly elevated. Which imaging study should be performed to localize the primary tumor?
A 35-year-old man presents with painless gross hematuria. CT urography reveals a 3-cm enhancing renal mass. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 28-year-old woman with no significant history presents with pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea after a long-haul flight. D-dimer is elevated and CTPA confirms a segmental pulmonary embolism. She is hemodynamically stable. What is the preferred initial anticoagulant?

A 50-year-old man presents with acute monoarticular arthritis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Joint aspiration reveals negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals. Which agent is first-line for the acute flare if NSAIDs are contraindicated?
